finding.summary: Newly lexable `A:A` / `1:1` REFERENCE tokens reach un-updated consumers that call parseRef/parseRange and will throw
finding.evidence: The grammar change makes `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B` lex as REFERENCE tokens everywhere, but only three call sites were given the `expandUnboundedRanges` guard (calculator, MemStore.buildDependantsMap, YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap). Every other consumer of REFERENCE tokens still parses them directly: `extractFormulaRanges` (parses each REFERENCE via parseRange for highlighting — the docs added in this diff *claim* it 'skips unbounded refs' although no code in the diff makes it skip), `toSrefs(extractReferences(f))` used outside those three sites, `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` (row/column insert, fill, copy-paste rewriting) and `normalizeFormulaOnCommit`. `parseRef('A')` / `parseRef('1')` throw 'Invalid Reference', so typing `=SUM(A:A)` in the formula bar or inserting a row near such a formula can throw an unhandled exception in the UI rather than degrade.
